narrative.overview: AssessCraft reads like a well-kept examinations ledger: white sheets on pale paper, slate ink, hairline rules, and a single green mark that means this is checked. The interface is a record of work done by agents and signed off by people, so numbers, statuses and citations are the content, and the chrome stays out of their way. Density is high and type is small. Most working text sits at 11–12px, with monospace reserved for figures, IDs, marks and codes so they line up and read as data. Surfaces are near-flat. Depth comes from a white sheet against slate paper and a 1px rule, never from dramatic shadow. Colour is semantic first: emerald for action and verification, amber for caution, rose for defects, sky for information. Nothing else competes.
keyCharacteristics: White sheet cards (12px corners, 1px slate rule, hairline shadow) on slate-50 paper.
One brand hue, emerald, carrying both primary action and "verified" status.
Monospace for every figure: marks, counts, IDs, CLO codes, scores.
Small, dense type (11–12px working size) with uppercase tracked micro-labels.
Semantic tinted chips (wash background + rule border + deep text) for every status.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: White text only ever sits on emerald-700 or darker; emerald-600 fails 4.5:1. Helper text is slate-500 or darker, never slate-400.

rules.name: The One Green Rule
rules.body: Emerald means "act" or "verified", and nothing else. Never use it for decoration, illustration, or a category label.

rules.name: The Tinted Chip Rule
rules.body: Every status is written as wash background + matching rule border + deep text of one semantic hue. Never a solid saturated status pill.

rules.name: The Earned Status Rule
rules.body: A green chip is computed, never asserted. If the data can't prove it, the chip goes amber or the figure shows an em dash.

rules.name: The Figures Are Mono Rule
rules.body: Any number a lecturer might compare (marks, counts, scores, IDs) is set in monospace.

rules.name: The Border Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: Interactive emphasis is a darker rule, not a bigger shadow. Shadows above hairline belong only to things that float over the page.

dos: Do derive every status, badge and "ready" claim from data on the page; when the data can't prove it, say what is missing.
Do use emerald-600 (#047857) for the single primary action in a view and for verified status, and nothing else.
Do set every comparable number in monospace.
Do write status as a tinted chip: wash + rule + deep text of one semantic hue.
Do build containers as white 12px-cornered sheets with a 1px slate-200 rule and hairline shadow on slate-50 paper.
Do signal hover on cards and secondary controls by darkening the rule to slate-300.
donts: Don't present fallback or placeholder text as an agent's judgement; label it.
Don't introduce a second brand hue, purple included.
Don't add gradients, glassmorphism or glow.
Don't use shadows above hairline on anything that does not float.
Don't use emoji as icons; use lucide-react at 14–16px, inheriting the text colour.
